convoLines.text: "Can I tell you something? I saw something in the woods I'm not telling anyone about."
They settle in like someone glad you're here.
They go very still. Not relaxed-still. Held-still.
"I'm not from Denver. I'm from Columbus, Ohio. I keep my head down. Old habit. It kept me alive before; it keeps me alive now."
Carol looks at you, level. "I told you the truth. You can keep poking it, but it's told."
They nod slowly, not quite done, not quite continuing.
"Still on their secret."
Something in them almost softens — then doesn't. Not yet.
"Alright. But I'm not carrying your stuff."
"A name. Okay." You say it out loud, trying the shape of it:
"Roles. Not ranks — promises."
You show them Greenbrier Shoots — where it grows, how to tell it apart. Their eyes widen. "I never knew that."
"Okay. We'll pick this up later."
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
"This was good." They mean it.
"When's the last time you really laughed? Don't look away from this."
"Stealing joy. I like that. We should steal more of it."
"There's more, but that's for another fire."
"Three days ago. Someone dropped a whole basket of tubers and we just stood there laughing. It wasn't even funny. It was the standing there."
"Still on the last time you laughed."
"Not right now. I've got my own things to handle."
"Sorry — I shouldn't load that on you. What's up?"
"Dominic is gone and the world just... continues. That's the part I can't stand."
You show them Wood Sorrel — where it grows, how to tell it apart. "Huh." They turn it over in their mind. "I'll remember that one."
"Sleep's gone strange. I clean up other people's messes quietly at odd hours now. Whatever gets me to morning."
"Well." A breath. "That's where things stand."
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
"Right. Go on, then."
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
"Is there someone here you don't trust? Be honest."
Their eyes flick, just for a second, toward the fire. "Noted. I'll watch too."
"I don't distrust anyone exactly — I just haven't finished trusting most of them yet. There's a difference. A slow one."
"Still on who you don't trust."
"Forget I said anything. What did you want? Seen worse."
"Good question." "Since Dominic died... I keep expecting to see Dominic at the fire. Stupid."
"I save the best bite for last. It doesn't bring anyone back. It just keeps my hands from shaking."
"Roles. Not ranks — promises."
"Anyway." A small smile.
You show them Goldenrod — where it grows, how to tell it apart. They nod slowly, committing it to memory. "Good to know. Really good to know."
"Sure. I'll be around."
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
"About that question — What's something you're good at that nobody here knows about? Anyway, that's me."
"Noted. Filing that under 'extremely useful.' The village needs that."
Their friendliness thins — still there, just held at arm's length.
"Still on what you're good at."
"Okay. Yeah. I trust you."
"Forget I said anything. What did you want?"
"You want to know about that? Okay." "Last time things were different. They always are." "Dominic always took the burnt piece. Said someone had to. I take it now."
"I clean up other people's messes quietly for Dominic, now. Feels right. Feels like the least I can do."
"Roles. Not ranks — promises."
"So." They look at the fire for a moment.
You show them Greenbrier Shoots — where it grows, how to tell it apart. A short laugh. "And I've been walking past it for weeks."
"Sure. I'll be around."
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
"This was good." They mean it.
"About that question — What's your first memory? Like, ever. The earliest thing."
"Three. That's young. The brain keeps what it needs, I guess."
The warmth pulls back a notch. They're weighing something.
"Still on your first memory."
"Sorry — I shouldn't load that on you. What's up?"
"You want to know about that? Okay." "You asked me that before. It's a different question now." "The Sorting. They just... took Caleb. Came back like nothing happened. It wasn't nothing."
"My part? I save the best bite for last and stay ready."
"So." They look at the fire for a moment.
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
"Roles. Not ranks — promises."
"Oh — okay. Later, then."
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
"This was good." They mean it.
"Okay, real question: what's the funniest thing you've seen since we got here? I desperately need it."
They laugh — really laugh, the first real one you've heard in days. "Okay. Okay, that's good. I needed that."
"Watch for this: It goes perfectly still and arches its back to the sun. Sunback, every time. It hunts by day — watch the open ground."

"I used to laugh easy, before. Now it has to climb over everything to get out. But when it does — when it actually gets out — it's the most honest thing I do all day. Everything else I'm performing a little. Not that."
"...What's that supposed to mean?" Their voice goes careful.
"Still on the funniest thing you've seen."
"Okay. Yeah. I trust you."
"Forget I said anything. What did you want?"
"Roles. Not ranks — promises."
Their eyes do the math before their mouth does. You can see the calculation happening.
"I don't actually want to belong somewhere. I want to be left alone. I was embarrassed. Everyone here was someone, and I was... that."
They glance at the fire, then back. The quiet doesn't seem to bother them.
"Sure. I'll be around."
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
"Mm. I tried the Greenbrier Shoots like you showed me. Didn't poison anyone, so that's a win."
There's an ease between you now — the kind that takes weeks to build.
"Well." A breath. "That's where things stand."
"Still on that plant lesson."
Something in them almost softens — then doesn't. Not yet.
"Sure — what's on your mind?"
"You want to know about that? Okay." "Huh. I answered that once — back when the answer was simpler." "You feel that? The air before a storm. That's the village right now."
"That's... pretty much all of it, honestly."
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
"Roles. Not ranks — promises."
"Right. Go on, then."
"It's been a while. Glad we circled back to what's been happening."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
"That thing you told me — the funny one, when I was desperate for it. I still think about it."
"Come see what I found. You won't believe it."
"Here. I made an extra." Karen presses something into your hand — a decent tool, oiled and kept. (Useful. Keep it.)
"Saw things with too many joints. Give them room. That's the whole lesson."
They nod slowly, not quite done, not quite continuing.
"Still on that personal stuff."
"Yeah? What's up?"
"Huh. Let me think about that." "That night — I stood down Loud-Eyes at the treeline — it ran. I keep hearing it when I try to sleep."
"I keep touching the spot where it grazed me. Like it'll explain itself."
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
"Alright — I should get back to it."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
